title: Delete a Note with the × on its Grip strip, with Undo
lede: Every Note shows a **Delete button** (×) at the right end of its Grip strip. A click deletes the Note at once and shows the **Undo toast** for 5 s; Undo brings the Note back exactly as it was, `z` included. The × is not a Press: it never Raises or drags, and it leaves focus where it was.

files.question: What does a press and a click on the × do?
files.summary: The × stops its pointerdown from reaching the Note, then its click calls `deleteNote`.
files.owns: The × button and when to guard against a double-click.

files.question: Why doesn't a double-click on the × delete a second Note?
files.summary: For 500 ms after a mouse delete, presses and clicks on Notes are swallowed in the capture phase.
files.never: Swallows presses outside Notes, such as on the Undo toast.
files.tested: Browser test: a double-click on a × over another Note.

files.question: In what order does a delete touch the two stores?
files.summary: `deleteNote` ends Editing if it was that Note, records the Note for Undo, then deletes. `undoDelete` restores, then hides the toast.

files.question: How does a deleted Note come back unchanged?
files.summary: `delete` keeps `topZ`; `restore` puts the same object back with its own `z`.
files.owns: The Notes and their Stacking order.

files.question: Where is the Note that Undo would bring back?
When does the toast show, take focus and hide?
files.summary: Shows while `lastDeleted` is set; its effect hides it after 5 s and restarts on a newer delete.
files.owns: The toast, its timer, and focus after a keyboard delete.

steps.title: pointerdown on the ×
steps.explain: `stopPropagation` keeps it from the Note's own handler, so there's no Raise and no Drag. `preventDefault` keeps focus where it was, for example in another Note being edited.

steps.title: click on the ×
steps.explain: The Note is recorded for Undo before it's deleted, and Editing ends first if it was this Note, so no phantom Editing is left. A mouse click (`detail > 0`) also starts the double-click guard.

steps.title: The toast shows and its timer starts
steps.explain: The effect is keyed on the `lastDeleted` object, so a newer delete clears the old timer and starts a new one. The inner element is keyed by the Note's id, so a newer delete is announced again.

steps.title: click Undo
steps.explain: The same object comes back, with its own `z`. `topZ` was kept on delete, so the restored Note's place in the Stacking order is still valid.

steps.title: The second press lands where the deleted Note was
steps.explain: The guard runs in the capture phase on `document`, before any Note sees the press. It swallows only presses on Notes, so the toast still works, and it removes itself after 500 ms.

steps.title: Enter on a focused ×
steps.explain: The focused × is removed, so focus falls to the body. The toast moves it to Undo, so the user keeps their place. A mouse delete leaves focus alone, because `activeElement` isn't the body. No double-click guard runs, because `detail` is 0.

notes.title: The × covers most of the `ne` resize corner
notes.detail: It sits 2 px from the top and right for looks, so only a 2 px sliver of the `ne` corner still resizes. The other edges and corners all work. Chosen by the owner after trying it.

notes.title: × on another Note doesn't end Editing
notes.detail: Clicking × on Note B while editing A keeps A in Editing and its caret. The issue only requires ending Editing when the deleted Note is the edited one.

notes.title: The double-click guard leaks between tests
notes.detail: It is a document listener that outlives the deleted Note, so `delete.browser.test.tsx` waits 500 ms after each test. Users can't hit this; the alternative, owning the guard in a component, was more code for no user-visible gain.

notes.title: Deleting replaces the Trash zone
notes.detail: #6 stays skipped. Its delete and restore half is built here, so a Trash zone would only need the drop target.
